lemonde.description: Dans ce documentaire réalisé par Thibaut de Longeville et Yanis Tiliouine, le rappeur qui a rempli deux fois le Stade de France raconte les coulisses sordides de son succès.

france24fr.title: Midterms 2026 : quand l'Iran se moque de la défaite de Donald Trump et des républicains
france24fr.description: Le pouvoir iranien s'est réjoui du sévère revers électoral infligé au parti républicain et à Donald Trump, qu’il présente comme un désaveu de la guerre contre l'Iran. Téhéran multiplie les piques et diffuse même des images générées par IA moquant la défaite du président américain. Tout en ironisant sur les "erreurs de calcul" de Washington, le régime redoute tout de même une reprise des frappes américaines.

france24fr.title: Midterms : changements en vue en Afrique ?
france24fr.description: Après la victoire des démocrates aux élections américaines, la politique africaine de la Maison Blanche va t-elle évoluer ? Le retour au pouvoir de Donald Trump a eu des conséquences très concrètes pour les habitants du continent, que ce soit pour la santé, les visas, les deals passés avec certains pays. Votre émission le rendez vous Afrique vous propose une plongée dans l'Amérique de Trump. Entre rupture brutale de l'aide, recomposition des rapports de force. Un changement est-il possible ?

france24fr.title: Corruption, dossier Epstein... les démocrates préparent une série d'enquêtes sur le clan Trump
france24fr.description: Devenu majoritaire au Congrès, le Parti démocrate a désormais les coudées franches pour lancer des enquêtes parlementaires sur l’administration Trump, sur fond d'enrichissement personnel du clan présidentiel.

france24fr.title: Éthiopie : Des milliers de déplacés privés d’aides humanitaires
france24fr.description: La reprise du conflit en Ethiopie a provoqué le déplacement de milliers de civils. Mais après des années de guerre et des coupes budgétaires drastiques, les organisations humanitaires se font rares dans les camps de réfugiés et de déplacés, laissant leurs habitants sans nourriture et sans espoir.

france24fr.title: Midterms : "Trump n'est plus une machine à gagner" pour les républicains
france24fr.description: Analyse de notre chroniqueur Gauthier Rybinski.

france24fr.title: Afrique du Sud : les townships au cœur des élections municipales
france24fr.description: Près de 30 millions de Sud-Africains sont appelés aux urnes pour renouveler leurs responsables municipaux, dans un contexte de fortes tensions sociales. Dans les townships, les habitants dénoncent la précarité et l'insécurité, des préoccupations susceptibles de peser sur le résultat du scrutin.

france24fr.title: Éducation, transports, santé... à quoi s'attendre pour la journée de mobilisation de jeudi ?
france24fr.description: Les organisations syndicales ont appelé les secteurs public et privé à se mobiliser, jeudi, pour la journée interprofessionnelle de grèves et de manifestations pour les salaires. France 24 fait le point sur les perturbations attendues dans les différents secteurs, notamment à l'Éducation nationale et dans les transports.

france24fr.title: Midterms 2026 : la victoire écrasante des démocrates prévisible ?
france24fr.description: La victoire sans précédent des démocrates lors des midterms du mardi 3 novembre est due à plusieurs facteurs que les experts exposaient déjà avant le début de la campagne, mais l'ampleur de ces résultats marque un réel tournant, qui pour le coup, n'était pas attendu. Les précisions de Pierre Gervais, professeur de civilisation américaine à l'Université Sorbonne Nouvelle et Claire Meynal, grand reporter au Point et auteure de "La guerre des Amériques".

france24fr.title: Midterms : la Chine disposée "à continuer à travailler avec les États-Unis"
france24fr.description: La Chine a qualifié mercredi 4 novembre les élections américaines de mi-mandat "d'affaire intérieure". La porte-parole des Affaires étrangère chinoise, Mao Ning s'est dite "disposée à continuer à travailler avec les États-Unis afin de préserver et d'appliquer l'important consensus dégagé par les deux chefs d'État" sur les questions d'intérêt commun et les sujets de divergence. Les précisions de Baptise Fallevoz, correspondant France 24 à Pékin.

france24fr.title: Midterms 2026 : quelle fin de mandat pour Trump ? Parlons-en avec A. Cohen, A. Hurst et A. Corpet
france24fr.description: Une vague bleue a déferlé sur le Congrès à l'occasion des élections de mi-mandat aux États-Unis, les démocrates s'emparant de la majorité des sièges à la Chambre des représentants comme au Sénat. Si la victoire était attendue, son ampleur est une surprise : des bastions conservateurs comme le Texas, la Caroline du Sud et le Kansas ont basculé. Une défaite retentissante pour Donald Trump, qui avait fait de ce scrutin un référendum pour ou contre sa personne.

france24fr.title: Midterms : les républicains de l'État du Wyoming conservent leur place
france24fr.description: Aux États-Unis, le conservatisme cowboy règne au Wyoming, un des États les plus républicains du pays. Là-bas, le Parti conservateur est donc resté au pouvoir lors des élections de mi-mandat qui se sont déroulées mardi 3 novembre, bien que les démocrates progressent grandement. Les précisions de Sylvain Rousseau, grand reporter France 24 et réalisateur du documentaire "Merci bien trump !".

france24fr.title: Midterms : "mes lasers spatiaux dans les élections n'ont pas fonctionné cette fois"
france24fr.description: La déroute de Donald Trump aux élections américaines de mi-mandat est aussi celle d'Elon Musk. L'homme le plus riche du monde a injecté près d'un demi-milliard de dollars pour soutenir des candidats républicains, sèchement battus mardi 3 novembre dans les urnes. Mercredi 4 novembre, Elon Musk, est apparu ironique face à la série de revers cinglants pour les républicains, considérant que ses "lasers spatiaux dans les élections n'ont pas fonctionné cette fois".

france24fr.title: Midterms : le démocrate Abdul El-Sayed devient le premier sénateur musulman des États-Unis
france24fr.description: Dans le Michigan, État industriel frontalier du Canada et où vit une importante communauté arabo-américaine, le médecin démocrate Abdul El-Sayed, issu de la gauche du parti, est devenu le premier musulman élu sénateur des États-Unis mardi 3 novembre, au terme d'un affrontement très serré et acrimonieux avec son adversaire Mike Rogers, ex-député républicain. Les explications de Sarah Andersen, envoyée spécial France 24 à Dearborn.

france24fr.title: Midterms : le nouveau Congrès va-t-il permettre un retour à l'équilibre des pouvoirs ?
france24fr.description: Les pouvoirs de Donald Trump vont être considérablement limités suite à la victoire des démocrates aux midterms ce mardi 3 novembre. Le président des États-Unis conserve cependant quasiment autant de liberté de manœuvre sur la politique étrangère. Les explications de Laurent Cohen-Tanugi, avocat aux barreaux de Paris et New York et essayiste politique.

france24fr.title: Midterms : féliciter les démocrates, une stratégie de Trump ?
france24fr.description: Les élections de mi-mandat, remportées par le Parti démocrate dans la nuit du mardi 3 novembre, n'ont pas encore été contestées par Trump qui a même félicité ses adversaires d'avoir "fait du bon boulot". Une stratégie se cache-t-elle dans cette déclaration surprenante et polie ? Les explications de Jérôme Viala-Gaudefroy, docteur en civilisation américaine, spécialiste de la rhétorique présidentielle et auteur de "Les mots de Trump".

france24fr.title: Midterms : les pays européens réagissent à la victoire des démocrates
france24fr.description: Au Parlement européen, une jubilation majoritaire se dessine suite à la victoire des démocrates aux midterms de ce mardi 3 novembre. Le ministre allemand de la Défense a qualifié cette victoire "d'historique", le Premier ministre espagnol Pedro Sánchez, a lui affirmé que la société américaine "a voté contre la haine, le sexisme (...) et contre le privilège des élites". Les explications de Caroline De Camaret, cheffe du service Europe de France 24 à Bruxelles.

france24fr.title: Midterms : les résultats illustrent la déroute des républicains à ces élections
france24fr.description: Le scrutin des midterms de ce mardi 3 novembre révèle la victoire flagrante des démocrates dans les "swingstates" où les projections étaient extrêmement serrées. Parmi ces États clés, les résultats sont sans appel dans le Maine, l'Ohio, le Michigan, l'Iowa ainsi que beaucoup d'autres. Les précisions de Jules Boiteau, journaliste à France 24.

france24fr.title: Midterms : les électeurs sanctionnent-ils les politiques de Trump par le vote ?
france24fr.description: Le scrutin des midterms qui ont eu lieu ce mardi 3 novembre est clair : les démocrates imposent une victoire écrasante face aux républicains. Aux États-Unis, les premiers sondages post-élections annoncent que sept électeurs sur dix souhaitent que le Congrès exerce davantage de contrôle sur le président Trump. Les précisions de Matthieu Mabin, correspondant France 24 à Washington.

Todeszahlen 2025: Demenz wird in Hessen häufiger zur Todesursache

Midterms in den USA: Die US-Demokraten jubeln. Der Rest der Welt auch?
zeit.description: Die US-Demokraten gewinnen, aber die Außenpolitik macht noch zwei Jahre lang Donald Trump. Was das für den Rest der Welt bedeutet. Und: Ist die Rentensteigerung gerecht?

zeit.title: Einsatz am Bahnhof: Herrenloses Gepäck am Ostbahnhof - zwei Bahnsteige gesperrt
Deutsche in Tirol: Lasst gefälligst die Piefke in Ruhe!
zeit.description: Unsere Autorin erlebt den Hass auf Deutsche in Tirol. Dabei wäre ihre Heimatstadt Innsbruck viel langweiliger ohne die Zugezogenen – und sogar ohne nervige Influencer.

zeit.title: Hermanos Gutiérrez: Zwei Brüder, zwei Gitarren, kein Gesang
zeit.description: Hermanos Gutiérrez sind die angesagteste Popband aus der Schweiz. Brad Pitt hört ihre Songs, Ryan Gosling trägt ihr Fanshirt. Aber Hits schreibt man eigentlich anders.

nzz.title: London verschärft das Aufenthaltsrecht – aber nicht für alle
nzz.description: Die britische Regierung will Arbeitsmigranten doch nicht zwingend zehn bis fünfzehn Jahre auf eine Aufenthaltsbewilligung warten lassen. Wer genug verdient und in gesuchten Berufen arbeitet, soll das Bleiberecht wie bis anhin schon nach fünf Jahren bekommen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die IV torkelt, der Sozialstaat wird zu teuer, doch der Ausbau geht munter weiter
nzz.description: «Tax the rich»: Der Bundesrat will das Geld für die angeschlagene IV bei den Erwerbstätigen holen und Gutverdiener ganz besonders schröpfen. Das ist der falsche Weg.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: 40 Tote bei Angriff auf ukrainisches Hilfszentrum +++ Melania Trump kündigt Treffen mit Ukrainern und Russen an
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Ebola-Ausbruch in Zentralafrika: Britischer Ebola-Patient aus Kongo nach Grossbritannien ausgeflogen
nzz.description: Die Weltgesundheitsorganisation (WHO) hat den Gesundheitsnotstand ausgerufen. Die Infektionszahlen steigen weiterhin an. Die wichtigsten Antworten zum Ebola-Virus.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Midterms 2026: Vance äussert sich zum ersten Mal zum Wahlergebnis +++ Demokraten könnten auf ihr bestes Resultat seit 2008 kommen
nzz.description: Die Amerikaner haben einen neuen Kongress gewählt. Die Republikaner verlieren ihre Mehrheiten im Senat und im Repräsentantenhaus. Alle Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Brandkatastrophe von Crans-Montana: Der Bundesrat gibt im Streit mit Italien über Spitalkosten nach
nzz.description: Die Landesregierung zahlt 1,5 Millionen Franken für die Behandlung italienischer Opfer in der Schweiz. Eigentlich müsste nach einem europäischen Abkommen Italien dafür aufkommen.

nzz.title: Die Demokraten erobern die Regierungen der amerikanischen Gliedstaaten
nzz.description: Nach den Midterms stellen die Demokraten zum ersten Mal seit 2010 die Mehrheit der Gouverneursposten. Ihre Kandidaten konnten sich auch in republikanischen Hochburgen durchsetzen.

nzz.title: Latinos, Junge und Gegner des Iran-Kriegs: Wahlentscheidend war die Proteststimmung in einzelnen Bevölkerungsgruppen
nzz.description: Was steckt hinter dem republikanischen Debakel in den Zwischenwahlen? Für Präsident Trump gibt es nichts zu beschönigen: Er hat mit seiner Politik entscheidende Wählergruppen vor den Kopf gestossen.

nzz.title: Die Demokraten feiern einen historischen Sieg bei den Midterms – das sind die fünf wichtigsten Erkenntnisse
nzz.description: Kein Fingerspitzengefühl bei der Kandidatenwahl, keine Angst vor muslimischem Shootingstar, eine misslungene Wahlkreisschiebung, wütende Jungwähler und grosse Wirtschaftssorgen. Diese Kräfte trieben die «blaue Welle» an.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Erneuter Angriff auf Flughafen in Riad gemeldet
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Weniger Strafzahlungen, mehr Zeit für die Klimaziele: Bundesrat Rösti kommt der Autobranche entgegen
nzz.description: Um ihre kriselnde Autoindustrie zu entlasten, will die EU die CO2-Vorgaben für Neufahrzeuge lockern. Nun zieht der Bundesrat nach – allerdings zu spät, findet die Autobranche.

nzz.title: Trumps Koalition zerbricht – im politischen Fundament der USA ist etwas in Bewegung geraten
nzz.description: Die Demokraten erringen in den amerikanischen Zwischenwahlen einen historischen Sieg. Junge Wähler und Latinos haben die Seiten gewechselt. Dahinter steckt womöglich mehr als Protest gegen Donald Trump.

nzz.title: Monatlich 1000 Franken für Junge, mehr Abzüge für Gutverdiener: So will Baume-Schneider die IV vor dem Bankrott retten
nzz.description: Der Bundesrat hat am Mittwoch die Vernehmlassung zur IV-Integrationsreform eröffnet. Die Reform soll die berufliche Eingliederung stärken und die IV finanziell stabilisieren.

nzz.title: Ein Mädchen ist oft in Streitereien verwickelt, Kinder haben Angst vor ihm. Dann fehlt es acht Monate lang in der Schule
nzz.description: Die Mutter hingegen sagt, ihre Tochter habe in der Schule ein Trauma erlitten. Sie fordert eine Umplatzierung in Zürich – und geht vor Gericht.

nzz.title: Jetzt muss auch noch beim Auslandangebot gschmürzelt werden. Durch eine schwierige Woche mit der SRG
nzz.description: Die Schweizerische Radio- und Fernsehgesellschaft steht, einmal mehr, im Kreuzfeuer der Kritik. Doch der Support alter Freunde ist ihr auch jetzt gewiss.

nzz.title: Hackerangriff traf neben Supermärkten auch französische Blutbanken
nzz.description: Beim jüngsten Cyberangriff auf europäische Infrastruktur in der Nacht auf Montag sind neben Detailhändlern auch die Kühlsysteme von drei regionalen Blutbanken in Frankreich beeinträchtigt worden.

observador.title: A esperança não é optimismo é uma decisão
observador.description: Vivemos tempos de cansaço, de más notícias e de futuro sempre adiado. Porque é que a esperança se tornou urgente, e o que fazemos com ela?

observador.title: Kremlin espera que Trump mantenha esforço de paz na Ucrânia
observador.description: Peskov diz que Moscovo espera que Trump "prossiga os esforços em favor da paz" na Ucrânia, mesmo após os democratas conquistarem o controlo do Congresso.

observador.title: Juízes defendem debate amplo sobre liberdade de expressão
observador.description: A diretiva europeia contra ações judiciais abusivas que silenciam o debate público já devia estar em vigor em Portugal. A ASJP alerta para o atraso e defende consenso na transposição.

observador.title: CIA ajuda Kiev, Rússia ataca. Trégua de Melania pouco mudou
observador.description: CIA mantém apoio vital e discreto à Ucrânia, apesar de Trump manter críticas a Zelensky. Rússia continua a sentir que tempo joga a seu favor. EUA focam-se agora no Irão e diplomacia está mais longe.

observador.title: Presidente executivo da EDP abandona cargo em 2027
observador.description: Miguel Stilwell de Andrade comunicou a indisponibilidade para um terceiro mandado enquanto presidente executivo. EDP prepara sucessão para 2027. Também Vera Pinto Pereira deixa a administração.

observador.title: "Estes estão a ser os dias mais difíceis da minha vida"
observador.description: Depois de várias horas de silêncio, o guarda-redes do Andorra que chocou com Jesús de Miguel reagiu pela primeira vez através de um comunicado e mostrou-se disponível para "enfrentar o que vier".

observador.title: "Qualquer edifício é uma oportunidade para fazer habitação"
observador.description: O projeto de restauro da Quinta de Crasto, em Vila do Conde, assinado por Nuno Valentim, venceu o Prémio Gulbenkian Património. Falámos com o arquiteto sobre habitação, turismo e o futuro das cidades.

observador.title: Porque dizemos “as chaves” para uma só chave? - Dúvidas
observador.description: Neste episódio de dúvidas, Marco Neves aborda ainda a utilização regional do “imos” e como aplicar o artigo antes de “português”.

observador.title: Primeira tempestade e ciclone? Vem aí uma semana de chuva
observador.description: Este ano não há Verão de S. Martinho, apesar de as temperaturas irem subir. Começa a chover esta sexta e só deve terminar lá para dia 13. Os dias piores são domingo e segunda, devido à possível Bruna.

observador.title: Flávio Bolsonaro chorou após resultados das eleições?
observador.description: Vídeo nas redes sociais alega mostrar Flávio Bolsonaro a chorar após derrota para Lula nas eleições do Brasil. Mas as imagens foram gravadas três dias antes da votação, durante a campanha eleitoral.

observador.title: 16h. Habitação. Governo vai reunir com grupos parlamentares
observador.description: Informação avançada pelo gabinete do Ministro dos Assuntos Parlamentares. Ainda, o PCP não tem grandes expectativas em torno do desfecho destes encontros.

observador.title: PSP ausente do festival neonazi por causa do Halloween
observador.description: A autarquia revogou a licença do evento na manhã de 31 de outubro, mas a PSP não enviou agentes para o festival, optando por concentrar meios nos festejos de Halloween. Caso vai ao Ministério Público.

observador.title: PS "sem linhas vermelhas", mas quer fim da renda moderada
observador.description: Na véspera da reunião com Montenegro, PS destaca cinco medidas na habitação — e garante que contas públicas não serão afectadas. Quer isenção de mais-valias na venda de segunda casa até 300 mil euros.

observador.title: Centeno pede "paciência" para a construção de habitação
observador.description: O antigo ministro das Finanças fala num "problema típico de crise de congestão", relacionando o aumento da procura de casas com a subida dos salários em Portugal. "Não temos oferta suficiente", diz.

observador.title: Sindicato acusa Governo de instrumentalizar ação policial
observador.description: "Os constantes ziguezagues do MAI, a leviandade perante decisões judiciais e a aplicação cega de regras transferem indevidamente o ónus da crise da habitação para os polícias", refere a ASPP/PSP.

observador.title: Portugal e Alemanha reforçam cooperação na Defesa
observador.description: Nuno Melo considerou a Alemanha "um parceiro estratégico fundamental" e "um aliado antigo" de Portugal. Cooperação bilateral surge num momento em que o país está a rever a Lei de Programação Militar.

observador.title: Carneiro sob pressão, entre a rua e o Governo
observador.description: Protestos pela habitação expõem diferenças no PS: há quem peça (e tenha) maior intervenção na rua, outros exigem distância da contestação. Líder quer manter pontes e endurecer crítica a Montenegro.

observador.title: IL sobre reunião em São Bento: "vai ficar tudo na mesma"
observador.description: A presidente dos liberais considera que "vai ficar tudo na mesma" na reunião marcada "a contragosto" por Luís Montenegro com o PS e o Chega. "Estes três partidos não se entendem", sublinha.

spiegel.title: Athen: Drei Studierende durch Molotowcocktails und Äxte verletzt
spiegel.description: Die Angreifer verfolgten sie mit Äxten und Molotowcocktails: Bei einem Zusammenstoß politischer Hochschulgruppen in Griechenland hat es Verletzte gegeben. Das Bildungsministerium verurteilt die Gewalt.

spiegel.title: Midterms 2026: Bedeutet der Sieg der Demokraten das Ende des Iran-Kriegs?
spiegel.description: Die Republikaner haben eine drastische Wahlpleite kassiert, auch wegen der Auswirkungen des Irankriegs. Wie sich das auf Trumps Angriffspläne auswirken könnte.

spiegel.title: Midterms 2026 in den USA - JD Vance: Für alle ist offensichtlich, warum wir verloren haben
spiegel.description: US-Vizepräsident JD Vance geht nach dem Wahldebakel der Republikaner offenbar auf Distanz zu Donald Trump. Eine Widersacherin des Verteidigungsministers triumphiert. Und: »MAGA Mike« Johnson schmeißt hin. Die Liveanalyse.

spiegel.title: Marius Borg Høiby muss doch erst mal weiter in Untersuchungshaft bleiben
spiegel.description: Ein Gericht wollte den Sohn von Norwegens Königin Mette-Marit aus der U-Haft freilassen. Doch ein Berufungsgericht kassiert die Entscheidung nun wieder ein.

spiegel.title: »Blutgräfin« Elisabeth Báthory: Wie aus einer ungarischen Gräfin eine blutbadende Bestie wurde
spiegel.description: Sie soll Dienerinnen die Lippen zugenäht, deren Fleisch verspeist haben: Die »Blutgräfin«, jetzt mit Isabelle Huppert im Kino zu sehen, gab es wirklich. Wer war die ungarische Adlige – und mutierte sie wirklich zum Monster?

spiegel.title: Trendsport Jugger: Marie, 13, spielt eine Sportart, die kaum jemand kennt
spiegel.description: Marie macht einen Sport, den kaum jemand kennt. Sie nimmt regelmäßig an Turnieren teil und gewann mit ihrem Verein, dem VfL Rethwisch, bereits drei deutsche Meisterschaften.

spiegel.title: München: Toter Junge in Hotelzimmer – Polizei ermittelt wegen Gewalttat
spiegel.description: Neben dem toten Kind in einem Münchner Hotelzimmer wurde auch eine Angehörige gefunden. Sie kam in ein Krankenhaus. Woran der 13-Jährige starb, ist unklar.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz reist nicht zur Klimakonferenz: Grüne kritisieren Kanzler als »Enttäuschung in Sachen Klimaschutz«
spiegel.description: Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz wird nicht zur Klimakonferenz in die Türkei reisen. Die Grünenfraktionschefin Katharina Dröge spricht von einem »verheerenden Signal für die Welt«. Kritik kommt auch von Luisa Neubauer.

spiegel.title: US-Midterms 2026: So historisch ist der Triumph der Demokraten
spiegel.description: Enorme Preise, Frust über Trump, hohe Wahlbeteiligung: Fast alle Schichten der US-Bevölkerung strafen den Präsidenten ab. Doch nicht nur das – die Grafikanalyse.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: US-Demokraten, Trumps Niederlage, Janosch ist tot
spiegel.description: Die US-Demokraten feiern ihren Sieg – und stehen vor einer harten Probe. Trump verliert die Wahl an der Tankstelle. Deutschland trauert um den Schöpfer der Tigerente. Das ist die Lage am Mittwochabend.

spiegel.title: Verbrenner-Aus: Umweltausschuss im EU-Parlament stimmt für Lockerung

phys-org.title: Speaking in a second language may shift your moral compass—but it can't overpower it
phys-org.description: In today's interconnected world, millions of people move between two or more languages every day. They may negotiate at work in one language, speak with family in another and follow news, entertainment and social media across several others.

phys-org.title: New species of pygmygoby discovered at the edge of the Red Sea's unexplored deep reefs
phys-org.description: Researchers have described a new species of fish from the northern Red Sea, found at the entrance to a cave on a steep reef slope. Charon's pygmygoby (Trimma charon) is a small, translucent fish with a broad orange-red stripe, golden spots on its tail and an unusual four-part eye. The two known specimens measure just 12 and 17 millimeters (0.47 and 0.67 inches).

phys-org.title: Intercropping could improve animal feed and reduce environmental impact
phys-org.description: Scientists at Nottingham Trent University, the International Centre for Agricultural Research in the Dry Areas (ICARDA) in Ethiopia and Ethiopia's Jimma University wanted to explore the benefits of growing oats and alfalfa together, as opposed to separately, and without irrigation or fertilizer. The research is published in the Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture.

phys-org.title: Pulsars set first mass limits on supermassive black hole pairs in the early universe
phys-org.description: So far, observations by instruments including the James Webb Space Telescope have revealed the presence of surprisingly massive black holes in the early universe. Even less than a billion years after the Big Bang, some of these bodies already weighed billions of times the mass of the sun, and to date, astronomers are unclear as to how they could have grown so large so quickly.

phys-org.title: A new tool helps target conservation and pollution control on the Ganges River
phys-org.description: An estimated 6 billion liters (1.6 billion gallons) of untreated sewage is discharged daily into the Ganges River Basin, home to 650 million people. Combined with seasonal monsoon flooding, the sewage and other pollutants, including agricultural runoff and industrial waste, create a major threat to public health.

phys-org.title: Tracing Darwin's finches' deadly new invader—the avian vampire fly
phys-org.description: Comprehensive genetic analysis has shed new light on the spread of an invasive, bloodsucking fly, which poses a devastating threat to the iconic Darwin's finches of the Galápagos Islands.

phys-org.title: From ABCs to geometry: Kindergarten readiness linked to math achievement through ninth grade
phys-org.description: Children's developmental readiness in kindergarten can predict their math achievement as late as ninth grade, according to research from the University of Toronto's Ontario Institute for Studies in Education (OISE).

phys-org.title: New modeling links gaps in Earth's geological record to rising and sinking continents
phys-org.description: Research led by a University of Wollongong (UOW) Ph.D. candidate may have solved one of Earth's most perplexing geological mysteries: What caused the Great Unconformity?

phys-org.title: Ancient DNA traces origins of English, German and Scandinavian languages
phys-org.description: English, German, Dutch and the Scandinavian languages are all members of the Germanic language group, spoken by hundreds of millions of people today. But where did these languages come from?

phys-org.title: Giant planet emerges from two-year-old JWST data thanks to glare-removal technique
phys-org.description: Even the world's most powerful telescopes have their blind spots. Although NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) can peer billions of years into the past, it still struggles to photograph planets orbiting nearby stars. Stars shine with such extraordinary brightness that their glare overwhelms nearby planets' faint glow.

phys-org.title: Researchers use seasonal satellite imagery to map shrub encroachment in Inner Mongolia grasslands
phys-org.description: Researchers from the Aerospace Information Research Institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (AIRCAS) used satellite images collected across the growing season to map shrub cover in the grasslands of Inner Mongolia, China. By tracking seasonal differences in growth, they were able to distinguish shrub patches from dense grass, which can look similar in a single image.

phys-org.title: Foot-stiffening socks could make walking less tiring
phys-org.description: Human feet are much stiffer than those of other primates, which means they limit midfoot bending during walking. The evolutionary reasons for this are not entirely clear. One idea is that the features that stiffen the foot evolved to make upright walking less effortful.

phys-org.title: Secrets of the avian calendar: When do migratory birds have the opportunity to reset their schedule?
phys-org.description: A team led by Vojtěch Brlík from Charles University in Czechia and the University of Guelph in Canada analyzed data from more than 2,300 birds tracked using miniature devices to find out how closely linked individual stages of the migratory birds' annual cycle are. The scientists were also interested in whether these linkages break down at a certain stage and whether late-departing individuals can make up for their delay.

phys-org.title: A new spin on catalysts: A roadmap for smarter chemical reactions
phys-org.description: Electron spin is a quantum property that makes electrons behave like tiny magnets. It can influence how electrons interact with each other and how chemical reactions take place. But what does this have to do with producing fertilizers, making cleaner fuels or improving energy technologies? What connects all these processes is the use of catalysts, materials that help chemical reactions happen faster and more efficiently. phys-org.title: Lecturers and students see AI use very differently, study finds

phys-org.title: Wild animals can now GPS-collar themselves for research
phys-org.description: For six decades, wildlife researchers have faced a persistent challenge: to attach a tracking device to study a wild animal, they first have to catch it. Now, a new approach developed at the Norwegian University of Life Sciences (NMBU) allows GPS collars to be deployed autonomously on free-roaming terrestrial wildlife. phys-org.title: Millions of bogong moths are blanketing cities in Australia, and they are still endangered
phys-org.description: In recent weeks, people across Australia have found fluttering bogong moths (Agrotis infusa) in their homes, cars and even bedrooms. These insects have embarked on their annual migration from breeding grounds across southern Australia to the cool caves of the Australian Alps.

phys-org.title: Seagrass helps Biscayne Bay's mangroves keep up with rising seas
phys-org.description: The mangroves of Biscayne Bay have been getting help from an unlikely neighbor—the seagrass meadows just offshore. Dead seagrass blades and seaweed drift loose until the tide carries them into the mangroves, where they pile up, rot slowly and then become part of the ground.

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

undark.title: The New Importance of the Scientific Seminar
undark.description: Opinion | The rise of artificial intelligence in science complicates the notion of expertise. When AI can be used to generate ideas, conduct research, and write papers, live scientific presentations — such as public talks and seminars — become more important as a way to demonstrate who is a real expert and who is not.

proj-syn.title: China Is Defanging the Dollar, Not Dethroning It
proj-syn.description: China offers Iran and Russia a way to circumvent US sanctions and continue doing business. But this comes at an elevated cost, because these countries are paid in onshore, non-convertible renminbi, which they must then convert into dollars using underground financial networks—tacitly reinforcing the greenback’s dominance.

proj-syn.title: A Fatal Challenge to Mainstream Economics
proj-syn.description: The intellectual project on which mainstream economists were raised, and which still forms the backbone of textbook education, has disappeared. What remains is a pastiche of attempted patches, apologies, and corruptions of “heterodox” ideas, all peddled by exponents of an “orthodoxy” that lacks a theoretical core.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Must Bail Out France
proj-syn.description: If France is to avoid default, the European Central Bank will need to buy large amounts of its government’s bonds through the Transmission Protection Instrument. But meeting this need—and preventing a potentially disastrous eurozone sovereign-debt-crisis—will require the ECB to waive its own rules.

proj-syn.title: The Rise and Fall of Privacy
proj-syn.description: Privacy is not a natural phenomenon, but rather a historical achievement. It emerged after the Reformation and the wars of religion that followed, reached a high point during the Victorian era, and has now been eroding for decades, long before the advent of the digital economy, social media, and AI.

proj-syn.title: Good Institutions Require Good People
proj-syn.description: Well-designed laws, courts, catechisms, extrinsic motives, social approval, and even a few good and decent people are of no avail if too many people do not behave like self-respecting and other-respecting adults. Childish pride and envy, grabbing more of the sweets, Donald Trump-style, do not make for a good society.

proj-syn.title: Oligarchic World Order
proj-syn.description: Today, some 64 heads of state or government are oligarchs, leading countries that together account for some 60% of global GDP. The question is thus no longer whether oligarchs will rule the world, but rather what kind of world they are building.

proj-syn.title: Poland’s Constitutional Civil War
proj-syn.description: Polish right-wing populists recently stormed the country's Constitutional Tribunal, winning applause from the Kremlin and far-right fellow-travelers across Europe. As in other countries, the constitutional tribunal is the institution that distinguishes a proper democracy from a dictatorship making it a target for authoritarians.

proj-syn.title: The Tech Brotherhood Wants Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: After centuries of nation-states, a new form of sovereignty is asserting itself. The small fraternity that controls the major digital platforms has already proven capable of even more intrusive and insidious forms of control than most states can muster.

proj-syn.title: The Far Right’s Vision for Europe
proj-syn.description: In many ways, Europe’s far right has already won, regardless of what happens at the ballot box in the coming months. Its parties may still quarrel among themselves, but they agree on the three big issues that will define much of the European political agenda for years to come.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Bright Future
proj-syn.description: A narrative of European decline has taken hold, and if the EU continues on its current path, it may well materialize. But this is not a foregone conclusion: Europe retains considerable strengths on which it can build as it pursues critical reforms aimed at unleashing innovation.

proj-syn.title: A Debtors’ Club for a Fragmented World
proj-syn.description: The newly created Borrowers’ Platform aims to facilitate knowledge-sharing and capacity-building among debtor countries, while amplifying their voices in global financial circles. But at a time when the Paris Club of sovereign creditors is increasingly unable to act collectively, the Borrowers’ Platform should ramp up its ambition.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Tariff Fiasco Could Save Free Trade
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump’s tariffs have raised prices and hurt businesses without reducing the trade deficit or creating manufacturing jobs. But global trade has held up better than expected, and growing public opposition to tariffs could pave the way for a retreat from protectionism.

proj-syn.title: If AI Thinks for Us, Democracy Will Suffer
proj-syn.description: Whereas the internet buried us in information, AI enables us to outsource analysis altogether. But when it comes to grappling with humanity’s most important questions, we must resist the temptation and recognize that we all have a duty—to each other and to ourselves—to keep “showing up.”

proj-syn.title: A Tory Mentor for the MAGA GOP
proj-syn.description: Kemi Badenoch’s keynote address at the British Conservative Party conference last month outlined her plan for a pro-growth future that respects fiscal discipline and human dignity. As American conservatives look beyond Donald Trump and to the 2028 primary campaign, they should embrace a similar agenda.

proj-syn.title: The Politics of Poland’s Judicial Crisis
proj-syn.description: The removal of Bogdan Święczkowski as president of the Constitutional Tribunal has triggered a physical confrontation at the court and a political standoff between Donald Tusk’s government and the far-right Law and Justice (PiS) party. But Święczkowski was not so much removed as barred, because he held the position illegally.

proj-syn.title: Mapping AI Resistance
proj-syn.description: Since a society that is reluctant to deploy a technology will not capture its gains, it is worth understanding why the AI revolution is being welcomed in some places and resisted in others. The explanation is not as simple as headline poll data and much media coverage suggest.

proj-syn.title: The World’s Perilous Ebola Complacency
proj-syn.description: The exponential trajectory of the latest Ebola outbreak is an urgent reminder that infectious diseases do not wait for ideal geopolitical alignments or balanced budgets. Global leaders must fund the Africa-led regional response today, or risk paying an immeasurably higher price in human lives and economic devastation tomorrow.

proj-syn.title: Industrial Decarbonization Is Good for Business
proj-syn.description: With major governments showing open hostility toward climate solutions or focusing on other needs, one might think that progress toward decarbonization is in jeopardy. Yet across the global industrial sector, many companies are increasing productivity, boosting revenue growth, and reducing emissions all at once.
